entries.proposition: WHAT THIS DOCUMENT IS. It states the controversy as a live two-sided question. This matters for how much weight the piece may carry: PMC deposits it as article-type 'editorial' with subject 'Editorial', and PubMed assigns publication type 'Journal Article' with NO Review tag. It is a 5-section, 17-reference opinion piece of 13,575 characters of extracted text, not a systematic review, and this repository must not weight it as one.
entries.snippet: The role of CFSs in cancer is debatable and two major views dominate the discussion in this regard

entries.proposition: AND IT ANNOUNCES ITS VERDICT BEFORE PRESENTING ANY EVIDENCE. The last sentence of the introduction commits the piece to one side of the two-sided question its own title asks. Paired with the framing locator, this fixes the genre: the passive view is stated in order to be set aside, and it is never given an advocate. MEASURED, not impressionistic: PubMed returns exactly ONE record in all of Cell Death Discovery, all years, with 'fragile' or 'FRA16D' in the title -- this one. The 'Current questions and controversies' series published no counterpoint.
entries.snippet: Here we discuss supporting evidence favoring active and tumor suppressor functions of WWOX in tumorigenesis

entries.proposition: THE OPPOSING VIEW'S OWN PREMISE, STATED FAIRLY AND THEN SET ASIDE. Hemizygosity is introduced as what licenses the passenger hypothesis, with the authors' own hedge ('although not proven') intact.
entries.snippet: Many of these deletions are hemizygous, suggesting, although not proven, that the other allele is maintained. This assumption led to the hypothesis that alterations in CFSs are secondary events that do not contribute to the multistep tumorigenesis process.

entries.proposition: PRINCIPAL FINDING 1 -- THE SAME OBSERVATION IS USED ON BOTH SIDES, AND THE PIECE NEVER RECONCILES THE TWO USES. Hemizygosity was the premise of the passenger hypothesis three paragraphs earlier; here the identical fact becomes evidence for haploinsufficiency, i.e. for the driver view. No argument is offered for why hemizygosity favours haploinsufficiency over passenger status -- the two uses simply sit in the same article. This is text-versus-text within one document and is declared text_only on both sides; nothing here is a panel reading. FIDELITY CHECK on the mouse clause, against PMID 17360458 held at complete_fulltext_read in this ledger: the datum transmits FAITHFULLY (spontaneous tumour-bearing 10/58 heterozygotes vs 2/60 wild type). The INFERENCE does not: that source's own haploinsufficiency conclusion is interpretive -- its tumours retain Wwox immunoreactivity, and protein positivity does not demonstrate an intact second allele or unchanged dosage -- and the editorial transmits the inference stripped of that declared interpretive status.
entries.snippet: Another interesting observation is that most of the deletions within WWOX are hemizygous rather than homozygous, suggesting haploinsufficiency. In support of this notion, Wwox heterozygous mice develop higher incidence of spontaneous tumors.
entries.anchor: Section 'Alterations of WWOX in cancers support its role as a tumor suppressor', paragraph 3

entries.proposition: PRINCIPAL FINDING 2, PART A -- THE CENTRAL STATISTIC AND ITS UNRESOLVABLE CITATION. The quantitative claim that carries the whole 'selective pressure' argument is cited to the ROOT URL of a project homepage: no accession, no dataset name, no GISTIC run identifier, no access date. The number is not reproducible from the citation given. An external anchor was sought before asserting anything about the value and none is offered by the source.
entries.snippet: the WWOX locus is the fifth most frequently deleted locus in 10 844 samples from 33 cancer types (Q-value=1.31E−266; http://www.broadinstitute.org/tcga/home)
entries.anchor: Section 'Alterations of WWOX in cancers support its role as a tumor suppressor', paragraph 1

entries.proposition: PRINCIPAL FINDING 2, PART B -- THE CALIBRATION SET UNDERCUTS THE INFERENCE IT IS OFFERED TO SUPPORT, AND THIS IS ARITHMETIC ON THE ARTICLE'S OWN PRINTED NUMBERS. Checked BOTH WAYS before being asserted. INTERNALLY COHERENT: by the quoted Q-values WWOX (1.31E-266) ranks below PTEN (0) and RB1 (7.24E-273), which is consistent with the claimed fifth place if two further unnamed loci also outrank it. BUT THE INFERENCE FAILS: TP53 -- the canonical tumour suppressor, offered here as calibration for what 'significantly deleted' means -- is quoted at 5.04E-22, some 244 orders of magnitude WEAKER than WWOX. If this metric ranked loci by tumour-suppressor importance, TP53 could not sit that far below WWOX. It does not: it ranks RECURRENT FOCAL DELETION, which is precisely what a common fragile site is expected to produce whether or not the gene inside it is a driver. THE STATISTIC THEREFORE CANNOT DISCRIMINATE THE PASSIVE HYPOTHESIS FROM THE ACTIVE ONE, and it is the piece's leading evidence for the active one. The 'single gene within the deleted peak' argument is the one part of this paragraph that does bear on driver status, and it is a peak-width argument, not a Q-value argument.
entries.snippet: Well-known tumor suppressors such as PTEN, RB1 and TP53 are significantly deleted (0, 7.24E−273 and 5.04E−22, respectively), although the deleted regions have additional genes within their peaks (i.e. PTEN with the tumor suppressor KLLN); WWOX, on the other hand, is a single gene within the deleted peak emphasizing that losing its own activity contributes to cancer
entries.anchor: Section 'Alterations of WWOX in cancers support its role as a tumor suppressor', paragraph 1

entries.proposition: PRINCIPAL FINDING 3 -- HOW THE PIECE DISPOSES OF A NEGATIVE THAT RUNS AGAINST IT: BY REFRAMING, INSIDE A SECTION HEADED 'support its role as a tumor suppressor'. McAvoy's result is that CFS alteration does not predict the associated gene product's expression -- a null that weakens the deletion-to-loss-of-function chain the whole argument needs. The gloss converts it into a claim that the alterations 'are not merely responsible' for WWOX dysregulation, i.e. into a call for additional mechanisms rather than a constraint on the existing one. The negative is neither refuted nor conceded; it is absorbed. PMID 18000379 is NOT held in this ledger at any depth, so this restatement could not be checked against its source and that is recorded rather than glossed.
entries.snippet: reported that there is no relationship between alteration of a given CFS and expression of its associated gene product in a given cancer, suggesting that these alterations are not merely responsible for dysregulation of WWOX protein expression
entries.anchor: Section 'Alterations of WWOX in cancers support its role as a tumor suppressor', paragraph 3

entries.proposition: THE PIECE CONCEDES BOTH CAUSES IN ONE SENTENCE, WHICH IS MORE HONEST THAN ITS CONCLUSIONS. Selective pressure AND fragility are named together as reasons for the deletion frequency. The Conclusions then assert that the loss is 'not a secondary/passive event because of the fragility of its locus', dropping the concession. Recorded because a reading that only collects a paper's errors is not reading it: this sentence is the piece's own best statement of the position its title asks about.
entries.snippet: WWOX is among the most significantly deleted genes in cancers,

entries.proposition: AN UNCHECKABLE LOAD-BEARING CITATION. Half of the induction claim -- the single-strand-break arm -- rests on 'unpublished data'. There is no route by which any reader, then or now, can verify it, and it cannot be entered into this repository at any epistemic level above IPOTESI. Recorded as a permanent limit of this source.
entries.snippet: levels of WWOX protein were recently shown to be induced following DSBs

entries.proposition: PRINCIPAL FINDING 4 -- THE MECHANISM MOST LIKELY TO BE CARRIED FORWARD BY A READER, AND THE CITATION FOR ITS FIRST STEP DOES NOT MATCH THIS REPOSITORY'S OWN RECORD. The chain is asserted as established fact and cited to refs 8 and 10. Ref 8 is PMID 25331887, held here at partial_fulltext_read: this repository's BLIND LOCATOR AUDIT of that paper's supplement struck the clause 'ITCH-dependent' from CLAIM 029's own text on the finding that it 'has no blot, lane, label or legend mention anywhere in this supplement'. Ref 10 is PMID 25245215, a REVIEW, unread in this ledger. And this repository's reading of PMID 23370280 assigns ITCH-dependent K63 stabilisation of WWOX to a DIFFERENT paper and mechanism, PMID 24550385 (complete_fulltext_read here), which the editorial does not cite. NOT a claim that the editorial is wrong -- 25331887's body was read under an earlier receipt and the audit covered only its six SI pages -- but the citation offered for the ITCH step points where this repository's own record does not. ONE THING IT GETS RIGHT AND IT IS WORTH SAYING: K63 here carries a non-proteasomal, trafficking-type role, which is the CORRECTED form of the textbook default in epistemic_discipline.md, not the false universal 'polyUb leads to the proteasome'.
entries.snippet: ITCH mediates K63-linked ubiquitination of WWOX and promotes its translocation into the nucleus where it activates ATM in a positive feed-forward loop manner

entries.proposition: FIDELITY CHECK, AND THIS ONE PASSES ON WHAT IT SAYS AND DROPS HALF OF WHAT ITS SOURCE SHOWS. Against PMID 23370280, held at complete_fulltext_read in this ledger: cytoplasmic retention and suppressed transactivation are transmitted FAITHFULLY. What is dropped is that source's headline -- WWOX competes with ITCH and thereby INCREASES DeltaNp63alpha abundance while lowering its activity, the demonstration that greater protein abundance can coexist with lower function. Under a heading 'WWOX promotes apoptosis' only the suppressive half survives. Incomplete, not false, and incomplete in the direction that serves the argument.
entries.snippet: WWOX interaction with ΔNp63α inhibits its nuclear translocation and suppresses its transactivation function

entries.proposition: AN EMPIRICAL CLAIM WITH NO CITATION AT ALL. The apoptosis section opens with an in vitro and an in vivo result and carries no reference; the section's first xref is ref 11, two sentences later. A reader cannot resolve which cell lines, which tumour models or whose data. Recorded because 'reviewed elsewhere' at least points somewhere and this points nowhere.
entries.snippet: Ectopic expression of WWOX in different cancer cell lines resulted in apoptosis in vitro and marked inhibition of tumorigenicity in vivo

entries.proposition: PRINCIPAL FINDING 5 -- DISPOSAL BY OMISSION, CHECKED AGAINST THE VERY REVIEW BEING CITED. The 'frequent loss' framing is attributed to PMID 24510053, which this ledger holds at complete_fulltext_read. That review's own content, as read here: 'WWOX loss is not the only direction reported. Some studies document INCREASED WWOX in breast, gastric and prostate carcinomas, which the authors read as complex regulation.' The editorial cites the review for the loss-only direction and does not carry the countervailing observation the review itself reports. The entire selective-pressure argument requires loss to be the rule.
entries.snippet: was originally cloned as a putative tumor suppressor because of its frequent loss in cancer
entries.anchor: Section 'Alterations of WWOX in cancers support its role as a tumor suppressor', sentence 1

entries.proposition: PRINCIPAL FINDING 6 -- THE ONE PLACE THIS PIECE TOUCHES THE REFERENCE GENOTYPE, AND THE CITED FACT RUNS AGAINST THE ARGUMENT IT IS OFFERED IN SUPPORT OF. The premise is that loss of a common fragile site carries no INHERITED selective pressure because cancer strikes after reproduction. The support offered is that GERMLINE WWOX loss of function causes neuronal disorders. But a germline loss-of-function phenotype is exactly what inherited selective pressure on that locus looks like, and it acts before reproduction, not after it. The second sentence contradicts the first; it is introduced with 'In support of this assumption'. This needs no external data -- the inversion is visible in the article's own two consecutive sentences. The neuronal claim rests on a single citation, ref 14 (PMID 25416187, Tabarki 2015), which is NOT held in this ledger at any depth; the two Aqeilan-authored reviews cited elsewhere in this piece cannot carry it, because this repository's complete read of PMID 24510053 measured ZERO occurrences of epilepsy, seizure, brain, CNS, WOREE, encephalopathy, ataxia, intellectual, recessive or syndrome across its 38,845-character body.
entries.snippet: One explanation might be that cancer usually occurs after the reproductive phase and therefore loss of CFS would not have an inherited selective pressure. In support of this assumption, germline mutations or loss of function of WWOX are associated with neuronal disorders,

entries.proposition: THE PIECE'S OWN THESIS, QUOTED SO THAT WHAT THE FIGURE DOES TO IT IS CHECKABLE. It asserts a single-sided resolution: not passive, actively contributing.
entries.snippet: we propose that WWOX loss early in the precancerous stage is not a secondary/passive event because of the fragility of its locus but provides a growth advantage that actively contributes to tumorigenesis

entries.proposition: THE PIECE'S STRONGEST SELF-LIMITATION, AND IT IS IN THE LAST PARAGRAPH. CFS expression is cell-type-specific, so behaviour is expected to vary between cancer types. This is the sentence that most constrains any transfer of the thesis to another tissue -- and a fortiori to a post-mitotic, non-neoplastic one. It is stated once, after the conclusion it qualifies.
entries.snippet: As the expression of these CFSs and their associated genes is cell-type-specific,

entries.proposition: SCOPE OF THE GENERALISATION, RECORDED BECAUSE IT NAMES THE COMPARATORS. Four further CFS genes are named as having DDR roles, with the hedge 'some having established tumor suppressor function' -- i.e. not all of them. None of the four is held in this ledger at any depth.

entries.proposition: PRINCIPAL FINDING 7, PANEL SIDE -- THE CAPTION'S DELTA SITS ON THE ELEMENT THE PANEL LABELS 'Passenger'. Read at native resolution and then adjudicated on a 400 dpi render of PDF page 2 before anything was asserted. On the right ('Extensive' replication stress) branch the panel draws exactly ONE open triangle, and it sits directly above a TRUNCATED DNA helix whose shaded field extends past the drawn duplex -- the deletion -- and the label beneath that helix reads 'Passenger'. The element labelled 'Driver' is a separate object: the WWOX protein oval struck through with a large X. The X is the panel's driver symbol and the caption never mentions it. So the caption attributes positive selection -- the driver property -- to the symbol the panel assigns to the passenger side, and the caption's '(depicted as Delta)' has NO referent anywhere on the driver side of the panel. CHARITABLE RECONSTRUCTION, STATED BECAUSE IT MUST BE: the authors may intend two distinct deletions, one in the locus and one in the gene. The panel draws one. On an article whose title asks whether the event is passive or active, the reader who trusts the caption and the reader who opens the figure get OPPOSITE assignments. Left branch, for contrast: the helix is drawn intact and unlabelled by any triangle.

entries.proposition: PANEL SIDE, QUALIFYING THE THESIS -- THE FIGURE IS LESS ONE-SIDED THAN THE TEXT. The Conclusions assert that WWOX loss is 'not a secondary/passive event'. The panel does not draw a choice between passenger and driver: it draws BOTH, side by side on the same 'Extensive' branch, assigning 'Passenger' to the locus break and 'Driver' to the loss of the gene product. That is a both-and model, and it is a better answer to the title's question than the text's either-or. Recorded as a qualification and not as a contradiction: the panel does not deny the thesis, it decomposes it.

entries.proposition: PANEL SIDE, QUALIFYING THE LOCUS NAME. The panel labels the fragile site 'FRA16' -- no terminal D. Verified at 400 dpi and again at 300% magnification of that render; the glyph sequence is F-R-A-1-6 and the label ends there. The article's title, body and caption all say FRA16D. FRA16 is not a fragile-site designation on its own: FRA16A, FRA16B, FRA16C and FRA16D are four distinct sites, so the panel's label is ambiguous between them while the text is specific. Small, and reported as small -- it changes no result. It is recorded because it is the article's own title object and because it is invisible to every check that does not open the image.

verbatim_locators.note: First read of this article; no prior receipt of any kind existed. 22 locators over 5 fingerprinted artifacts: 19 text locators on the XML, 3 figure locators on the pixels. The reading's product is concentrated in six findings — the double use of hemizygosity, the Q-value calibration that cannot discriminate the hypothesis it is offered for, the absorption of the McAvoy negative, the ITCH citation, the loss-only framing contradicted by the very review cited for it, and the reproductive-phase argument whose supporting fact runs the other way — plus the caption-versus-panel symbol assignment on the article's only figure.
